correctness.rationale: On (0,1], φ(1)=0, φ(0+)=∞, φ'<0 and φ''>0 so the bivariate strict Archimedean copula exists. For f=φ+log t, f'(t)+tf''(t)=(t-1/2)²>=0; double integration gives f(uv)-f(u)-f(v)+f(1)>=0, implying φ(uv)>=φ(u)+φ(v) and hence C(u,v)>=uv globally. Differentiating implicit generator equation gives density c(u,v)=ell(u)ell(v)k(C)/ell(C)^3, with ell=-φ' and k=φ''. The fetched verification code performs exact Fraction root brackets using a bounded log-series remainder and monotone density enclosures: -0.019002196<Δc(1/4,1/4)<-0.019002192<0. Independent high precision direct evaluation gives approximately -0.019002193959, and independent symbolic first-order defect is -11/576. Reflected-density criterion of the original paper makes the C not PMI. Analytic PQD and exact PMI sign proof are separate and unrestricted on the unit square.

final_claim: The smooth strict bivariate Archimedean copula with generator φ(t)=-log t+t/4-t²/4+t³/9-1/9 is PQD everywhere but not PMI; its reflected density difference at (1/4,1/4) is negative in (-0.019002196,-0.019002192), refuting PQD⇒PMI in the Archimedean conjecture.
limitations: The decisive finite-parameter sign uses exact rational logarithm remainder enclosures, not raw numerical approximations.
